paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of high relative density Ti-48Al-1Fe alloy using irregular blend powder

evidence.quote: The Ti-48Al-1Fe alloy was prepared via vacuum pressure-less sintering, and the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties during the sintering densification process of the mixed powder system were investigated.

The blend powders were mixed in a mixer for 8–12 hours at 150 rpm.
Subsequently, the powder mixture was pressed at 250 MPa for 10 minutes using CIP.
The temperature is then raised to 600–800 °C and held for 3–5 hours to complete the dehydrogenation reaction.

After this process, the material is sintered in a high vacuum environment with a vacuum degree of 10^-3 Pa. The samples were heated to different temperatures (1000 ℃, 1100 ℃, 1200 ℃, and 1300 ℃) for 3–5 hours.
Furthermore, HIPed samples are obtained by non-capsule HIP of sintered samples at 1250 °C for 3–5 hours. The resulting sample was labelled as HT1300.
TiAl3, TiH2 and Fe powders are mixed with D50 particle sizes of 20.2 μm, 20.4 μm and 23.3 μm respectively.
The green body was sintered and insulated at two temperatures of 600 ◦C 800 ◦C and 1300 ◦C. The final relative density of the sintered sample reached 98.3 ± 0.14%.
HIPed samples are obtained by non-capsule HIP of sintered samples at 1250 ◦C for 3–5 hours, the relative density could be increased to more than 99.9%.
